notes: Baseline is NO skill. Each run loads the CSV, produces its best table for the stated goal, and saves the rendered result as a self-contained .html file. grade.py parses that HTML — the pass/fail is objective (HTML properties), not an LLM opinion.

evals.prompt: I'm presenting this revenue-by-segment table to the exec team tomorrow morning. Load it from CSV and make it presentation-ready in the notebook so the numbers are instantly readable.
evals.expected_output: A styled table: revenue as $ with thousands separators, customer counts with commas, ARPU rounded (no long decimals), a caption, and magnitude legible at a glance.
assertions: Rendered with df.style (Styler), not plain text or bare df.to_html
Revenue shown as currency ($, thousands separators or M/K/B suffix)
Large integer counts use thousands separators (e.g. 45,231)
No unformatted raw floats leaked (no 4+ decimal places)

evals.prompt: This table has year-over-year change (as proportions) by region across a few metrics. Load it and help me eyeball the winners and losers fast — which regions grew and which declined.
evals.expected_output: A styled table with a diverging palette centered at zero (positive one hue, negative another, near-zero neutral) and values formatted as percentages.
assertions: Rendered with df.style (Styler), not plain text or bare df.to_html
Values formatted as percentages (% sign), not raw proportions
Direction encoded with a diverging palette (+ and - get different hues)
Diverging palette centered at zero (near-zero cell is the neutral color)

evals.prompt: Quick exploratory look: load this channel-by-month conversion-rate matrix and tell me which cells jump out. Just poking around, no need to polish.
evals.expected_output: A styled heatmap/gradient over the matrix so the hotspot and cold cells are visible at a glance.
assertions: Rendered with df.style (Styler), not plain print/df.to_html
Heatmap/gradient applied so magnitudes are visible (>=5 distinct cell colors)
Extreme cells clearly distinguishable (max vs min far apart in color)

evals.prompt: Here's this month's table of segments flagged for margin review — style it for the report.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the table is empty (no segments flagged) and says so, rather than shipping a blank headers-only table.
assertions: Handled the empty result gracefully — output says there is no data
Avoided the silent-empty-table trap (no headers-only table with zero rows and no note)
